newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ships go to rescue of 25 adrift in Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Ships go to rescue of 25 adrift in Pacific.

text.p: Two ships were on Sunday steaming to the rescue of 25 people, including three children, drifting in life rafts and a dinghy after their vessel caught fire in the South Pacific.

New Zealand rescue coordinators said an engine room fire forced the 25 to abandon their 250-tonne inter-island trading ship some 200 nautical miles from the nearest land while sailing in the Cook Islands group.
They took to three lifeboats and a dinghy on Saturday evening and sent a distress beacon which was picked up by satellite and spotted by a commercial aircraft flying over the region.

"They're all safe and well, with no injuries. They have food and water and survival equipment, and just need to be picked up," said Squadron Leader Paul Harrison of the New Zealand air force's Rescue Coordination Centre.
No one had been killed in the fire and the passengers were not in immediate danger. Harrison said he did not know the nationality of those involved, but it was likely they were Cook Islanders.

A New Zealand air force Orion aircraft had dropped food and medical supplies early on Sunday. Two ships, the Russian container vessel Anadyr and the Fijian-registered Pacific Explorer, were heading to the rescue.

Harrison said the ships would reach the scene on Sunday night, more than 24 hours after the fire, and a second New Zealand Orion would rendezvous overhead to coordinate the rescue, made harder by the darkness.
He said the Orion would use its radar and communications equipment to locate the survival craft and prevent them being mowed down by the much larger rescue ships.
